And for one such as I, time means nothing.|IG-88|}} '''IG-88B''', also commonly known simply as '''IG-88,''' pronounced '''Eyegee-Eightyeight''', or as a '''Phlutdroid''', was a rogue, deadly [[Gender|masculine]] [[IG-series]] [[assassin droid]] manufactured by [[Holowan Laboratories]] who, because of his desire to kill [[Species|organic beings]], worked as a [[bounty hunter]]. Following the [[Battle of Hoth]], he and several other bounty hunters were summoned by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] to the ''[[Executor]]'' and hired to track down the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' and its [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel]] crew. Unable to track his quarry, IG-88 trailed his chief rival, [[Boba Fett]], to [[Bespin]], where the bounty hunter destroyed the assassin droid; however, IG-88 was later rebuilt. At some point, IG-88 undertook a software infiltration into [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]], but his plan was single-handedly thwarted by [[R2-Q5]]. Decades later, the droid met with [[mercenary]] [[Bazine Netal]] to speak about the location of the ''Millennium Falcon''. ==Biography== ===Origins=== {{Quote|This notorious IG-series assassin droid possessed an unstoppable desire to hunt and kill his prey, earning him a reputation as one of the top five bounty hunters in the galaxy. It also earned him access to some of the best-paying clients, like Darth Vader and a wide variety of Hutts.|R0-GR|''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]''}} [[File:IG88Cover-AgeSpecial1.png|thumb|right|300px|IG-88 gained infamy as one of the most feared and effective bounty hunters of the Imperial Era.]] Created in secret by [[Holowan Laboratories]]{{ForceCollection|IG-88B|star=2}} shortly after the [[Clone Wars]] as the first{{SideshowCite|set=Sideshow Collectibles|text=Sixth Scale Figures|pack=IG-88|altlink=https://www.sideshowtoy.com/collectibles/star-wars-ig-88-sideshow-collectibles-1000292}} of five identical [[IG-series]] [[assassin droid]]s,''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' IG-88B, more commonly known as simply IG-88, and also known as a Phlutdroid, realized his skill and desire to [[Death|kill]] the moment he was first activated and turned on his creators, [[Holowan Laboratories massacre|killing everyone in the lab]]. After serving as a [[Battle droid|war droid]] for a [[time]], IG-88 elected to take on a career in [[bounty]] hunting because it gave the droid a chance to murder more [[Species|organics]] and to earn [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. In doing so, IG-88B also distracted attention from reaching [[IG-88A]], who embarked on a plan to [[IG-88A's plan to overthrow organic life|overthrow organic life]].{{HelmetCollectionCite|2|Weapons & Uniforms}} From that moment on, he became one of the most feared [[bounty hunter]]s in [[the galaxy]] in part due to the lingering fear of [[droid]]s from the Clone Wars, particularly those capable of [[Battle droid|battle]] and [[assassin]]ation. Feeding into his unquenchable thirst to hunt and kill and gaining notoriety comparable only to that of [[Boba Fett]], his chief rival,''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' IG-88 was able to take on jobs from well-paying clients, including a wide variety of [[Hutt]]s and the [[Imperial Era|reigning]] [[Galactic Empire]]. In time, his reputation placed him amongst the five best bounty hunters working in the galaxy. ===Age of the Empire=== ====Capturing Qi'ra==== {{Quote|Oh, Qi'ra, Qi'ra. It does look like you have fallen into our little trap. Catching you was quite difficult, my young friend. I had to partner with IG-88 here.''"
"''A Crimson Dawn Lieutenant will fetch a nice bounty.|Hondo Ohnaka and IG-88|}} [[File:FODTriplecross.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Qi'ra as prisoner of IG-88 and Hondo before she tricks them both.]] Around [[11 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Triplecross]]" to around [[11 BBY]]. IG-88 teamed up with [[Hondo Ohnaka]] to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Qi'ra)|collect]] the [[bounty]] on [[Crimson Dawn]] [[Lieutenant (criminal)|lieutenant]] [[Qi'ra]]'s head. Tracking Qi'ra down, IG-88 and Hondo managed to apprehend Qi'ra. Turning the bounty hunter and the [[pirate]] against each other, Qi'ra convinced IG-88 to collect the bounty on Hondo instead of the bounty on her. Attacking Hondo, IG-88 was quickly [[stun]]ned and put in [[Stuncuffs|binders]]. After Qi'ra had similarly tricked and apprehended Hondo, IG-88 was led away by Qi'ra so that she could collect the bounty on his head. ====Hired by Kallus==== {{Quote|You're certain this is where we'll find the individuals involved in the rebel activity on Savareen? I don't like being disappointed, bounty hunter.''"
"''Yes. I am certain.|Kallus and IG-88|}} Sometime later, IG-88 was hired by [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] to assist in tracking down [[Imperial Army]] deserter turned smuggler, Captain [[Han Solo]] of the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. ====Seeking a data-tape==== {{Quote|What is ''that''?''"
"''IG-88. An ''actual'' bounty hunter. Also, probably interested in your data tape. He's good—one of the best in the galaxy. And he's a surprise. Take cover!|Leia Organa and Sabine Wren|}} Later, IG-88 [[Mission to Garel|pursued]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] on [[Garel]], seeking a [[data-tape]] in her possession of [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] base locations. Organa was assisted by [[Sabine Wren]], who identified the droid, and the pair fled as the assassin opened fire in the corridors of [[Garel City Spaceport]]. However, Wren planted a [[paint bomb]], surprising IG-88 and covering him in purple paint. Leia convinced several [[stormtrooper]]s to fire at the bounty hunter, and the droid was hit by a blast before retreating.{{FOD|Bounty of Trouble}} ====Apprehending a thief==== {{Quote|To kill is reward enough.|IG-88, to an Imperial captain|}} IG-88 was hired by an [[Unidentified Imperial captain (IG-88)|Imperial captain]] to capture a thief named [[Venga Liss]] who hijacked a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] on a [[jungle]] planet. Eventually, the droid killed Liss when he detonated the shuttle. IG-88 later allowed himself to be destroyed and taken to the headquarters of the [[Gillanium Syndicate]], where he killed the group's leader and Liss' father, [[The Underlord]]. ====Capturing the Gatto Gang==== {{Quote|IG-88! This deadly droid had been given the task of capturing the sneaky Gatto Gang.|[[CR-8R]]|{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=9|story=Tales from Wild Space: IG-88 vs. the Gatto Gang}}}} [[File:IG-88_hunting_Gatto_Gang.jpg|thumb|right|265x265px|IG-88 during the hunt for the Gatto Gang.]] At some point during the reign of the Empire, IG-88 was hired by [[Duke]] [[Blazor]] of the [[Black Sun]] to capture the [[Gatto Gang]] that consisted of [[Sylvestarr]], [[Ziggee]], and [[Moggee]]. Although the Gatto Gang tried to trick him, IG-88 eventually captured all three of them. Between [[2 BBY]] and [[4 ABY]],"[[A Rebel Bounty]]" takes place after [[Alexsandr Kallus]]'s betrayal in "[[Zero Hour]]" but before [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba's]] death in {{Film|VI}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. ''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' places the events of "Zero Hour" seventeen [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], which occurred in [[19 BBY]] according to ''Galactic Atlas'', meaning that "Zero Hour" takes place in [[2 BBY]], and "A Rebel Bounty" takes place between 2 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] and 4 ABY. IG-88 kidnapped [[Grand-engineer]] [[Lony Coleema]] and brought Coleema to the abandoned [[Holowan droid foundry]], intending to learn the secrets of [[technopathy]] and details about secret Imperial projects.{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|annual=2020|story=A Rebel Bounty}} [[File:Ig88_05.jpg|thumb|left|250px|IG-88's remains sit in a Cloud City junk room]] By the [[Standard year|year]] [[0 ABY]], IG-88 consorted with the [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. He was present in the [[Hutt]]'s [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] while Jabba received [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. The [[Sith Lord]] told the Hutt to dispense with his audience, and IG-88, along with fellow hunters including Fett and [[4-LOM]], departed from the court.[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] ====Hired by Neeva==== {{Quote|His office is on the seventy-fourth floor, it'll be a fight the entire way up!|Neeva, to IG-88|''[[Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge – Last Call]]''}} In [[3 ABY]],The flashbacks in ''[[Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge – Last Call]]'' featuring IG-88 take place concurrently to {{Film|V}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates to [[3 ABY]]. IG-88 was hired by [[Neeva]] to kill [[Boggs Triff]] on the 74th floor of [[Boggs Triff's base]] on [[Nar Shaddaa]]. IG-88B was hired for this task because Neeva's brother was captured by [[Boggs Triff]]. IG-88 accepted the bounty and found the remains of other bounty hunters. IG-88B faced [[Boggs Triff's mob]] on the journey up to the 74th floor. Ruthlessly, IG-88 defeated every one of the members which attempted to kill IG-88. IG-88 eventually made it to the 74th floor of [[Boggs Triff's base]] and killed Triff by damaging a container, causing it to fall, crushing Triff almost instantly. ====Hired by Vader==== {{Quote|There will be a substantial reward for the one who finds the ''Millennium Falcon''. You are free to use any methods necessary, but I want them alive.|Darth Vader to IG-88 and several other bounty hunters|}} Immediately after completing the bounty, IG-88 answered a call put out by Vader for bounty hunters to track down the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. He and several other hunters, including Boba Fett, [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], [[Dengar]], [[Zuckuss]], and [[4-LOM]], assembled aboard the ''[[Executor]]'', where Vader offered a [[bounty]] for the live capture of [[Han Solo]] and his companions. IG-88 tailed the ''Millennium Falcon'' along with Fett to [[Cloud City]] on the [[planet]] [[Bespin]], where the assassin droid was defeated, destroyed,{{HelmetCollectionCite|2|Weapons & Uniforms}} and left for scrap after Fett, his longtime rival, caught it trailing him. Ultimately, Boba Fett captured Han Solo for Vader, who then later on delivered the bounty to Jabba on [[Tatooine]].{{Film|VI}} ====Hired to kill Vader==== {{Quote|Reports indicate you recently suffered structural compromise, Lord Vader. I am envisioning an enjoyable outcome to this encounter.|IG-88, to Darth Vader|}} Sometime later, IG-88 was hired by [[Sly Moore]] to kill Vader alongside the [[Droid Crush Pirates of Bestoon]]. She also informed him of the Sith Lord's damaged state and gave him the code needed to slice into his armor. Vader and the accompanying Sith assassin [[Ochi|Ochi of Bestoon]] were both lured into an ambush by a Hutt named [[Bokku]], who sent them after the pirates in an attempt to locate the recently stolen Han Solo. Upon arriving at [[Zee-Nine City Seven]], Vader and Ochi's ship was sabotaged, causing them to crash. They were then attacked by IG-88 and the pirates. During the firefight, IG-88 warned Vader that his mechanics were in worse shape than the droid's. [[File:VaderClaimsRemote-2020DarthVader13.png|thumb|right|300px|Darth Vader claims the remote control from IG-88, giving the Sith Lord control over the droid.]] When Vader told IG-88 that he had information he required, the droid responded that Vader would have to download it from his severed head. Vader went to destroy the droid, but IG-88 then used a remote to breach Vader's armor, gaining control over the Sith Lord. As he forced Vader to hold his lightsaber to his head, the Sith ordered IG-88 to tell him who had given him the code. The droid replied that the terms of his employment prevented him from sharing the information. While IG-88 was distracted, Vader used the Force to take the remote from him, allowing him to use it against the droid and force him to blast himself in the head. Once IG-88 was subdued, Vader and Ochi forced the pirates to retreat and used one of the droid's hands to access a terminal he had been using, allowing them to discover various dead ends the droid had been chasing, as well as the symbol of crime syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]]. After repairing himself, IG-88 returned to Coruscant and reported his loss to Moore and her [[Umbaran's Court|court]]. The droid lamented that Vader could not be defeated, but Moore assured him that Vader could only defeat them one at a time. And if they all stood together, then they would be more powerful than either Vader or Sidious could ever imagine. After uncovering Sly Moore's betrayal, Vader and Ochi returned to Coruscant to find her, her court, and IG-88 in [[Administrative Temple Garden 313A]]. Vader then struck down IG-88 once again before chasing Moore and her court into the Imperial Palace.[[Darth Vader (2020) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 14]] ====Hired by Crimson Dawn==== IG-88 was found on a planet by [[RB-919]], who decided to rebuild him. After being rebuilt, IG-88 was hired by [[Deva Lompop]]. IG-88 then killed RB-919 and his crew to test himself. He claimed RB-919's ship and contacted Lompop, under orders from [[Lady]] [[Qi'ra]] of Crimson Dawn. His mission was to re-acquire Solo from Fett's ship. As he tracked down ''[[Slave I]]'', he began to experience unpleasant flashbacks of his defeat at Lord Vader's hands. He then came under attack by several pirates who wanted his ship. IG-88 was able to to find ''Slave I'' on Tatooine and boarded the ship, but was quickly confronted by Fett, leading to a shootout in which the droid was able to subdue his opponent. However, Fett ruptured a piece of machinery on his ship which carbon-froze the droid. IG-88 was left behind while Fett continued to Jabba's Palace. IG-88 was able to free himself from the carbonite and Lompop's contract. He then returned to the planet RB-919 to contemplate his future and improve his programming. ====Hired to hunt Crimson Dawn==== {{Quote|You promised mercy if I surrendered!''"
"''That offer expired eight seconds ago.|A [[Unidentified Son-tuul Pride leader|Son-Tuul Pride leader]] is killed by IG-88|}} Sometime later, IG-88 took a bounty from the Empire for the leaders of the [[Son-tuul Pride]], who had been aiding Crimson Dawn. After [[Mission to Son-tuul|tracking]] the [[Rodian]]s to the [[Son-tuul Spaceport]], IG-88 gave them 25 seconds to surrender. When they fought him, IG-88 killed them and reported his success before taking another bounty for [[Vukorah]], leader of the [[Unbroken Clan]].[[Bounty Hunters 29|''Bounty Hunters'' 29]] ===Infiltrating the Death Star II=== At some point before or during [[4 ABY]], IG-88 undertook a software infiltration of the Empire's [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]]. However, his plan was single-handedly thwarted by the Imperial [[astromech droid]] [[R2-Q5]].{{ForceCollection|R2-Q5|star=3}} ===Contacted by Bazine Netal=== {{Quote|…We would have apprehended the ''Millennium Falcon''.''"
"''But you didn't.''"
"''Correct.|IG-88 and Bazine Netal about the time when he nearly captured the ''Falcon'' with Kallus|}} [[File:BazineNetalandIG-88.jpg|thumb|right|249x249px|Netal and IG-88 discussing the ''Millennium Falcon'']] In [[34 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]] to [[34 ABY]]. at some point after the [[Battle of Takodana]], IG-88 was contacted by the [[mercenary]] [[Bazine Netal]] to discuss the location of the ''Millennium Falcon'' after she heard a rumor about the time IG-88 nearly caught the ''Falcon''. During their rendezvous, IG-88 took the opportunity to tell Netal when he almost caught the ''Falcon'' with Kallus. IG-88 told Netal that he almost caught the ''Millennium Falcon'' again, but lost out to Fett. Netal responded that, though he had a lot of excuses, her employer only paid for results. She informed IG-88 that someone knew where the ''Falcon'' was and that they would tell her where it was before leaving him to continue with her search. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|The Besadii are not enemies you want to make."
"They are enemies ''you'' do not want to make, Corellian. I quite like enemies.|Dengar and IG-88|{{StoryCite|story=No Time for Poetry|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}}} [[File:GalaxyEdgeEnhancedEdition-IG-88-hunt.png|thumb|left|300px|IG-88 was an efficient and focused droid bounty hunter.]] A rogue''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]'' [[Class four droid|Class four]] assassin droid, IG-88B was obsessed with hunting, destroying and killing as a result of his incompletely formed droid programming. He tended to hunt alone and earned a reputation as a merciless hunter. His underlining motivation for being a bounty hunter was little more than his desire to hunt and kill organic beings. A hideous, battered chrome war droid, IG-88 stood 1.96 [[meter]]s in height. His steady aim, along with his ability to track targets with advanced [[sensor]]s that ringed his head and allowed him to see in all directions, won him great success. These sensors included multiple [[Color|red]] [[photoreceptor]]s, a [[heat sensor]] and a [[Audio sensor|sound sensor]]. IG-88 also had a [[Vocabulator|vocoder]] at the base of his head. His torso was able to fully rotate on the battlefield, allowing him to blast enemies on all sides. His tough metal body allowed him to survive most attacks without taking any damage and featured [[acid]]-proof [[Servomotor|servo]] wires. ==Equipment== {{Quote|Your opponent is IG-88…a Holowan Laboratories ''Phlutdroid'' armed with pulse cannons, concussion discs, vibroblades and a DAS-430 Neural Inhibitor.''"
"''And a ''double-prong'' gatalang ''armor piercer!''|[[Gak-Sixtoo]] and Ochi|}} [[File:ArmedToTheTeeth-SoH.png|thumb|right|250px|IG-88B carried a veritable arsenal of weaponry]] IG-88B carried an arsenal of weapons, including [[blaster rifle]]s, [[pulse cannon]]s, a [[DAS-430 Neural Inhibitor]] and a [[needle dart gun]] that launched [[poison dart]]s. The assassin droid also equipped himself with a modified [[DLT-20A blaster rifle]], a modified [[E-11 medium blaster rifle|E-11 blaster rifle]], and a [[vibrocleaver]].{{Legion|set=IG-series Assassin Droid Operative Expansion}} However, his most dangerous weapons were hidden inside his slender frame,''[[Star Wars Builders: Droids]]'' including a [[flamethrower]], a [[sonic device]] and [[toxic gas dispenser]]s. IG-88 also wore an ammunition [[bandolier]] that carried his [[concussion disc]]s and [[vibroblade]]s. As an IG-series droid, he was designed to have [[blaster]]s built into each [[Limb|arm]], installed sometime prior to the search for the ''Millennium Falcon''. IG-88 owned a modified [[Aggressor-class Assault Fighter|''Aggressor''-class Assault Fighter]]''[[Allies and Adversaries]]'' called the ''[[IG-2000]]''.{{Armada|set=Rebellion in the Rim|cardname=IG-88B}} ==Behind the scenes== ===Design=== {{Quote|IG-88 was never going to be more than a filler for the now infamous bounty hunter Lineup. I decided we needed a real dirty, evil, and vicious bot. Like the bounty hunters of old. Lots of weapons and protection. Dark and oily. So we made him big- 7'8"ish tall. Had to drop him down a level on set to get him in shot. Lean, but strong. In short, a killer. We started with the head. Then with all the bits, we had the rest. It just came together to us until was just right. No, some of the grown-ups were not taken with the idea. It was taking a different direction from the other bots, but I thought it should. And when someone said, "I don't think you would find a robot like that on a spaceship," my reply was, "You would on mine." The rest is history.|Bill Hargreaves, on designing IG-88|{{SW|url=news/interview-bill-hargreaves-former-jawa-scavenger-and-galactic-prop-man|text=Interview: Bill Hargreaves — Former Jawa Scavenger and Galactic Prop Man}}}} [[File:IG88_concept_btm.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Early concept art of the "chrome war droid" by Ralph McQuarrie.]] IG-88B, originally referred to as a "chrome war droid" in the script and also called "Phlutdroid" during production,{{DB|droid|ig88|IG-88}} was originally created for the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. His mechanical puppet was constructed by [[Bill Hargreaves]] and [[Steve Short]] of the props team and special effects department,''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]'' whose design was a complete departure from concept artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s streamlined, if not elegant, version. IG-88's cylindrical head was originally a combustion chamber in a [[Wikipedia:Rolls-Royce Derwent|Rolls-Royce Derwent]] jet engine, which was previously used as part of the distillery setup seen in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].{{SW|url=news/5-recycled-star-wars-props-and-costumes|text=5 Recycled ''Star Wars'' Props and Costumes|nolive=1}} McQuarrie would revise his earlier IG-88 design during the production the [[1983]] [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. Considered an "assassin droid," it did not appear in any version of the film's screenplay but was for the basis for [[EV-9D9]],''[[Star Wars Art: Ralph McQuarrie]]'' another practical droid built by Hargreaves and Short. McQuarrie's early concept art of IG-88 later inspired the design of the [[IG-RM bodyguard and enforcer droid]].{{SW|url=news/back-from-the-drawing-board-part-2-repurposed-star-wars-technology|text=Repurposed ''Star Wars'' Technology - Back from the Drawing Board, Part 2|nolive=1}} ===The mysterious portrayal=== [[File:BountyHunters_CloudCity.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Later McQuarrie concept art of IG-88, which eventually evolved into the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] character [[IG-72]].]] While [[Lucasfilm]] has no official record of the identity of the technician that operated IG-88 in ''The Empire Strikes Back'',{{InsiderCite|49|Trail of the Bounty Hunters}} the official ''Star Wars Authentics'' website has credited the role to Bill Hargreaves.{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsauthentics.com/iSynApp/productDisplay.action?sid=1102083&productId=1547290&isynsharedsession=Z3cbTSxXmbBGJrgVXj_lkjgVuGaP8D6nNq5-z8UbsKpEdaSACl02r4aCDzYhNvUm|text=IG-88|quote=Bill Hargreaves as IG-88 in ''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back''.|archivedate=20191011234353}} However, the online database [[Wikipedia:IMDb|IMDb]] instead credits Paul Klein as the puppeteer of IG-88, as well as that of [[BG-J38]] and EV-9D9 in the ''Return of the Jedi''. Despite this, there is no Paul Klein credited as a member of ''The Empire Strikes Back''{{'s}} effects crew. As IMDb often relies upon unconfirmed information submitted by fans and ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' was unable to determine who submitted said information, it is currently unknown whether or not Klein actually operated IG-88. Oddly, ''Star Wars Authentics'' credits Klein in place of Hargreaves in the description of the photograph titled "Darth Vader, Dengar, IG-88 and Boba Fett," despite having credited the latter in the descriptions of nearly every other live-action image of IG-88 available for purchase on the website.{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsauthentics.com/iSynApp/productDisplay.action?sid=1102083&productId=1136075&isynsharedsession=UG8nAifmZPQkna3IODDJ9qLhl-Cji-ZeEdY_ymdEW41EdaSACl02r4aCDzYhNvUm|text=Darth Vader, Dengar, IG-88 and Boba Fett|quote=David Prouse, Morris Bush, Paul Klein and Jeremy Bulloch as Darth Vader, Dengar, IG-88 and Boba Fett in ''The Star Wars: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back''|archivedate=20200811065935}} One fan wrote into the [[Rebel Rumblings]] section of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' to report with certainty that Klein was not the technician behind IG-88's operation. The fan identified themself as Shaun Shuey from Wonder Lake, Illinois, who claimed to be friends with Klein; according to Shuey, Klein was a then-19 year old fan who jokingly added himself to the Internet Movie Database as the technican behind IG-88, taking advantage of how only C-3PO and R2-D2 were given credits. According to Shuey, Klein was reading through ''Star Wars Insider''{{'s}} prior report on the possible technicans behind IG-88 while in a resturant with Shuey, who stated Klein jumped out of his chair upon seeing himself listed as a lead. Overall, Shuey concluded they had at least made their friend's day. While the ''Insider'' team was already doubting whether Klein was actually the droid's operator, Shuey's letter put their only lead on the case to rest.{{InsiderCite|52|Rebel Rumblings}} ===''The Mandalorian''=== Pre-release information for the [[2019]] [[Disney+]] live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' stated that [[IG-11]] was often mistaken for IG-88 [[in-universe]],{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/2019/08/25/the-mandalorian-character-details|text=''The Mandalorian'' 5 new character details|author=James Hibberd|date=2019-08-25|archivedate=20191112185028}} though IG-88 is never referenced in the show's [[The Mandalorian Season One|first season]].[[The Mandalorian Season One|''The Mandalorian'' Season One]] Orange-colored stripes and a double bandolier were added to IG-11's design to help distinguish him from IG-88. Concept supervisor [[Christian Alzmann]] gave IG-11 hands to better enable him to use his blaster [[rifle]]s, which is a detail that IG-88 was lacking.{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-1-guide|text="The Mandalorian" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} ===Non-Canon history=== ====Freemaker Adventures==== IG-88 appeared in the ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures]]'' [[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures Season Two|Season Two]] episode "[[Return to the Wheel]]," which premiered on [[August 3]], [[2017]]. He and several bounty hunters including Dengar, Bossk, 4-LOM and Zuckuss [[Mission to obtain an energy matrix activator|captured]] the [[Freemakers/LEGO|Freemakers]] but they escaped after [[Kordi Freemaker/LEGO|Kordi]] created a fight between the droid and organic bounty hunters.{{FreemakerAdventures|Return to the Wheel}} ====''Lego Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga''==== {{Quote|Have you seen a runaway rancor keeper? A big gentleman, prone to perspiration. He fled during the chaos at Jabba's palace and I have been instructed to bring him in. His name is Malakili. I have tracked him to this town. But the residents do not like to cooperate with a droid. If you provide assistance I will share the reward.|IG-88 greets the player in ''Lego Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga''|''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]''}} IG-88 appears in the [[2022]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' during an adaptation of his scene from ''The Empire Strikes Back''. The droid later appears in [[Mos Eisley]], a large [[spaceport]] on Tatooine, where he asks the player if they have seen a runaway [[rancor]] keeper. He explains that [[Malakili]] fled during the [[Rescue of Han Solo|chaos]] at Jabba's palace and he has been instructed to bring him in. He then asks the player to provide assistance in the quest "Green Harvest." Per IG-88's instructions, the player speaks to locals to find a lead on Malakili's location and passes the information to IG-88. The player eventually learns that Malakili was opening a [[restaurant]] in Mos Eisley. The player and IG-88 regroup at the restaurant and IG-88 blasts the door open. Malakili welcomes them into his [[Crystal Moon Restaurant]] and asks if he can take their order. The droid tries to captures Malakili, who explains that he assumed Jabba's death meant he had no one to work for, causing IG-88 to realize no one will pay him for the bounty hunting he's been doing. The droid decides to leave Malakili to his [[tato wrap]]s and then thanks the player, offering to provide their assistance as repayment.
